reviewer: Astra Max algebra agent; independent of original analysis author and root rewrite
scope: Independent mathematical, statement, rubric, formal-contract and source review. No candidate model evaluation; no new compilation claimed by this review.
checks: The task permits arbitrary real topological vector spaces and the Lean objects are continuous real-linear functionals. No norm, inner product, Hausdorff, local-convexity or completeness assumption occurs.
IsTopologicalAddGroup adds continuous negation only as a standard consequence of the stated continuous scalar multiplication at minus one; this is not a mathematical restriction.
Finite paths encode every finite cycle and include the zero-length anchored path. The potential is an actual EReal supremum, not an assumed optimizer or certificate.
Cyclic monotonicity bounds every closed path and forces the anchored value to be zero. Appending an arbitrary graph record proves finite values throughout the graph.
Every path is a continuous affine function, so the actual supremum is lower semicontinuous and its real-height epigraph is convex. No joint topology on the dual or separation theorem is used.
The subgradient proof uses finite graph values and translates by a real number, so no undefined infinity subtraction is used. The lower-bound path excludes minus infinity at every point.

The supporting-potential induction proves comparison against every normalized competitor, and therefore the constructed admissible function is pointwise least. Antisymmetry proves strict uniqueness, including infinite values.
The singleton-graph strict-extension example is independently present on actual real objects in Lean and is not an extra answer requirement.

The statement supplies definitions and the main target without the path-supremum route. The rubric accepts applicable classical theorems and other complete proofs, with no hidden length or vocabulary requirement.
